title: Reachable configurations admit bounded-window representatives
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be a binary input, let $S$ be a natural number, and let $sp$ be a space-bound function. Suppose every run of $N$ on any input $y$ using any finite choice word visits at most $sp(|y|)$ distinct work-tape cells in total, and $sp(|x|)\le S$. For every configuration $C$ reachable on input $x$ in the sense that its state, input-head position, work tapes, work-head positions, and output summary agree with those of some run, there is a configuration $D$ whose work heads lie within distance $S$ of the origin and whose work tapes are blank outside that window, with the same state, input-head position, work tapes, work-head positions, and output summary as $C$, and with the same configuration code at window size $S$.
hypotheses_covered: every run on every input and choice word uses at most $sp$ of space
